AC-3 Red and its container appear only on failure or fault states; running, waiting and paused use neutral or primary tones.

AC-4 The page shows exactly the same sections, fields, controls and labels as before, and every endpoint, poll and action behaves identically (existing tests green, unchanged except where they assert markup).
AC-5 tests/test_orchestrator_dashboard.py passes; privacy gate PASS; the assets reference nothing external.

report.objective: Bring the orchestrator workbench to the product's own Material 3 language and make the provider legible at a glance: Claude-run movements carry a warm orange accent, Codex-run ones a blue accent. Product Owner directive 2026-09-14: the workbench should look like the product it serves and be easier on the eye. Behaviour, data and endpoints are untouched.
output_contract: A workbench that looks like the product and separates Claude from Codex at a glance.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A self-contained restyle of three static files against a named token strip, with a clear do-not-touch boundary.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Presentation only: if a change would alter what the workbench reports or how it behaves, stop and leave it.
Run only tests/test_orchestrator_dashboard.py plus the privacy gate.
No external URL, no web font, no CDN reference anywhere in the assets.
Mechanical mismatches between this packet and the code are settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Commit early and often. SESSION_CLOSE names the token set, the two provider tokens with their values and measured contrast, and the test counts before and after.
risks: Restructuring the page while restyling it, so the operator has to relearn it.
Hard-coding the provider colours at the call site instead of as tokens.
Using a warning colour for a movement that is merely running.
Pulling a web font or an icon set.

in: Replace the flat palette with a Material 3 token set in dashboard.css: a surface family (surface, surface container, surface container high, outline, outline variant), an on-surface family (on-surface, on-surface variant), primary and its container, plus the semantic colours the console needs (success, warning, error, and their containers), all as CSS custom properties defined once at :root. Keep the dark scheme as the default and derive it from the product's token strip rather than inventing a second palette. Every colour used anywhere in the file must come from a token; no literal hex outside :root.

Material 3 shape and type: card-like surfaces with the M3 corner radii, an elevation expressed as surface-container tone rather than heavy shadows, 8-point spacing, and a type scale (title, body, label) applied to the existing elements. Do not restructure the page: the same sections, the same table, the same controls, the same order.

Provider accent: a token per provider (claude and codex) applied as a left edge or chip on each movement row and to the provider line, so a glance separates them -- Claude warm orange, Codex blue. Both must reach at least 4.5:1 contrast against the surface they sit on for their text form, and the accent must not be the only signal: keep the provider name in text (accessibility, and the product's own rule that colour never carries meaning alone). An unknown provider falls back to a neutral token.

State colour discipline: map the existing health and stage vocabulary onto the semantic tokens so that red means failure or a real fault only; a movement that is merely running, waiting or paused uses neutral or primary tones, never a warning colour. Keep every existing label's text exactly as it is.

Small legibility wins inside the existing structure: tabular numerals for the token, cost and duration figures; a monospace token only where an identifier is shown; consistent column alignment; a visible focus ring on every interactive element.

Update tests/test_orchestrator_dashboard.py where it asserts markup or class names, and add a small test that every colour literal in dashboard.css appears only inside the :root block (the token discipline above) and that both provider tokens are defined.
out: Any change to scripts/orchestrator_dashboard.py's endpoints, derived fields, polling, actions, stuck detection or data shape; new dependencies, a build step, web fonts or an icon library (the console is served as three static files and stays that way); a light-theme toggle; new columns or new information.
